summary: Iteration 8 — compliance X1–X7 backend tested end-to-end with 31 pytest cases (all passing serially). Covered: age gate (under-13/adult/minor/invalid DOB/consent/duplicate), /api/legal + consent persistence (verified via /users/me/export), data export shape + own email, account deletion full flow + owner guard (and guide owner guard, non-destructive), blocking cycle (feed hide, start-direct 403, both-direction message 403, blocks list, unblock → messaging restored, self-block 400), priority report categories (csam=priority:true, spam=priority:false, mod-only /moderation/priority), expanded report target types (invalid=400, post/comment/message/user/room=200), /reports/mine feedback with resolve → status/resolution, moderator post removal → /moderation/actions/mine entry + appeal success + 403 for someone-else + 409 double-appeal + /moderation/appeals, mute logs 'muted' action. Regression: guide/demo login, feed, post+like+comment, circles+search, rooms, events, wallet, self-gift 400, 7-day mute cap, private-circle gating, conversation IDOR 403.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1971 lines — recommend splitting into routers (auth, circles, posts, conv, rooms, wallet, moderation, compliance) before adding more features.

DELETE /users/me is non-atomic across ~15 collections on standalone Mongo. A partial-failure (e.g. network blip mid-delete) can leave orphaned data (gifts, event_rsvps, moderation_actions, appeals etc.). Consider a soft-delete + background purge or a cleanup worker to guarantee eventual consistency. Also note: moderation_actions, appeals, gifts, event_rsvps, room_messages, notifications are NOT removed on account deletion — intentional for audit, but worth documenting.
/moderation/priority and /moderation/appeals both gate on user.is_moderator only; circle-level mods have no priority queue. Fine for now, but note the asymmetry.

Report created with target_type='user'/'room' doesn't look up a circle_id, so /circles/{id}/reports will never surface them. Consider a global /moderation/reports fallback list (which does exist) — document the UX implication for circle mods.
Register rate limit is 5/minute per IP — correct & intentional, but parallel test runners share one IP in this preview. Documented in the test harness via retry/sleep.
seed_data_creation: Used existing guide/demo seed. Throwaway TEST_* users created per-test for destructive flows (deletion, blocking, appeals, mute). No seed data mutated beyond mod actions on throwaways; guide still owns seed circles.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Register endpoint is rate-limited to 5/min per source IP. When running pytest in parallel (xdist 2 workers), concurrent register calls will trip 429s. Either (a) run with `-o addopts=''` to disable xdist, or (b) use the built-in 429 retry helper in test_iter8_compliance.py `_register()`. Email is normalised to lowercase on register — assertions must `.lower()` compare. Guide account owns ALL seed circles so `DELETE /users/me` as guide always 400s (owner guard); use throwaway users for destructive tests. The under-13 DOB computation uses `datetime.now(utc).date()` so a 10-year-old DOB is reliably <13 regardless of leap-day edge cases.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no backend bugs found. Initial 7 test failures were test-harness issues (register 429 under parallel execution + an email-case assertion), fixed in the test file. After serial run, 31/31 pass in 133s.
